gap: A (boat): at 10-15 m the boat must read as a detailed, crewed vessel moving through water. Required: a modelled hull with windshield, railing and cabin detail; a visible occupant; a raised bow wave with a spray sheet at the hull; and a turbulent white foam wake that widens and breaks up over at least 2-3 boat lengths behind it. The flat white halo around the hull and the straight, even foam band must be gone.

- render_gate never refused a run.. Judge: The commercial frame wins all four pairs clearly (B, B, B, A), and no pair was close. The in-development frames do have strengths: fairly convincing mirror reflections of the towers, a plausible teal water colour, and real activity in the form of several boats leaving V-shaped wakes. The aerial harbour in pair 2 is the strongest of them. However, all four frames still look like a blockout. The towers are repeated boxes with tiled window decals, the ground is a flat untextured brown plane, the trees are simple lollipop shapes, and the promenades are empty, with no people, street props or traffic detail. Beyond the city the world ends in a flat plain at a hard horizon. Lighting is flat and even, with no sun direction, no glare and only a uniform beige haze. Where water meets objects, the wakes are smooth decal-like strokes with no spray, surf or foam breakup. None of the frames has a hero subject or a cinematic camera, and pair 3 is also cluttered by a HUD. The commercial frames win on four things together: real backlight with layered atmospheric haze, dense and varied environment detail out to the horizon, turbulent whitewater and spray, and dynamic framing around a detailed hero. In order of priority, the in-development build needs: (1) environment density and fidelity out to the horizon, with no empty ground plane; (2) a visible sun, specular glare on the water and haze in depth layers; (3) turbulent foam, spray and surf wherever boats or the shore meet the water; (4) hero assets and camera framing. None of the in-development frames wowed me. Three of the four commercial frames did: the lighthouse, the helicopter over the city, and the backlit train.
